newsitem.title: GERMANY: German parliament passes tougher deportation rules.
newsitem.headline: German parliament passes tougher deportation rules.

text.p: Germany's lower house of parliament passed a draft law on Thursday aimed at making it easier and faster to deport foreigners convicted of violence.
It was prompted by clashes between militant Kurds and police earlier this year, when hundreds of people were injured, and drawn up shortly after by Chancellor Helmut Kohl's cabinet.

The bill reduces the minimum jail sentences of which a foreigner must be convicted to face expulsion, to three years from five. It also adds aggravated breach of the peace to the list of crimes for which someone can be deported, regardless of the length of the sentence they receive.
It will now have to be approved by the upper house or Bundesrat, but will face opposition from the Social Democrat Party (SPD) which has the majority there.
Members of the SPD, the environmentalist Greens and the former communist PDS voted against the bill in the Bundestag, or lower house.

Interior Minister Manfred Kanther of Kohl's Christian Democratic Union told parliament: "The public will not accept it if Germany gives protection and residence rights to politically persecuted foreigners while this protection is abused by a small violent minority."
Hundreds of people were taken into custody and hundreds more injured when police tried to stop Kurds from attending a banned demonstration in the western city of Dortmund in March.
Authorities blamed the run-ins on the outlawed Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK) which they accuse of bringing to Germany their guerrilla war for autonomy in southeastern Turkey.
If the bill is rejected by the Bundesrat, the next step would be for a mediating committee of lower and upper house representatives to find a compromise solution.
The SPD called the measures overdone and ineffective and warned of opposition in the Bundesrat.
The measures passed on Thursday also provide for some improvements in foreigners' rights to counterbalance the tougher deportation rules.
For example a foreign spouse will be able to claim the right to permanent residency after one year instead of three and young people will be able to receive residency permits sooner.
The immigrant population in Germany numbers around seven million, 2.2 million of whom are Turkish citizens.
